title: Ezana adopts Christianity
description: King Ezana is converted by Frumentius, making Aksum one of the first states to become Christian.

title: Kaleb invades Himyar
description: King Kaleb crosses the Red Sea and overthrows the Jewish king of Himyar, the height of Aksumite power.

title: Muslim refugees received at Aksum
description: Followers of Muhammad fleeing Mecca are given shelter by the king of Aksum, the first migration in Islam.

title: Queen Gudit lays waste to Aksum
description: By tradition a queen named Gudit destroys Aksum and its churches, closing the Aksumite period.

title: Rock churches of Lalibela
description: Eleven churches are cut from the living rock, by tradition under the Zagwe king Lalibela.

title: Solomonic dynasty founded
description: Yekuno Amlak overthrows the Zagwe and founds the line, claiming descent from Solomon, that rules until 1974.

title: Amda Seyon's campaigns
description: The emperor defeats the Muslim sultanates to the east and greatly enlarges the Christian kingdom.

title: Battle of Shimbra Kure
description: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim of Adal defeats the imperial army and goes on to overrun most of the highlands.

title: Battle of Wayna Daga
place: Wayna Daga, east of Lake Tana
description: Emperor Gelawdewos, with Portuguese musketeers, defeats and kills Ahmad ibn Ibrahim, saving the Christian kingdom.

title: Susenyos turns Catholic
description: The emperor's public conversion under Jesuit influence sets off revolts that end with his abdication and the expulsion of the Jesuits.

title: Gondar founded
description: Fasilides builds a permanent capital with stone castles, the seat of the emperors for two centuries.

title: Era of the Princes begins
description: The murder of Emperor Iyoas by his minister leaves the emperors as figureheads of regional warlords for 86 years.

title: Tewodros II crowned
description: Kassa Hailu defeats the last of his rivals and is crowned emperor, reuniting the country.

title: Battle of Magdala
description: A British expedition sent to free hostages storms the emperor's fortress, and Tewodros kills himself.

title: Battle of Gura
description: Yohannes IV defeats an Egyptian army for the second time, ending Egypt's attempt to conquer the highlands.

title: Addis Ababa founded
description: Menelik and Taytu settle at the hot springs below Entoto, which becomes the capital.

title: Treaty of Wuchale
description: Menelik II cedes Eritrea to Italy in a treaty whose Italian text claims a protectorate over Ethiopia, the cause of the war that ends at Adwa.

title: Treaty of Addis Ababa
description: After its defeat at Adwa, Italy recognises Ethiopia as an independent state.

title: Railway reaches Addis Ababa
description: The line from the port of Djibouti is completed, giving Ethiopia its outlet to the sea.

title: Haile Selassie crowned
description: Ras Tafari Makonnen is crowned emperor and gives the country its first written constitution the next year.

title: Italian invasion
description: Italian armies cross from Eritrea without a declaration of war and take Addis Ababa in May 1936.

title: Haile Selassie appeals to the League
description: The exiled emperor asks the League of Nations to act against Italy and is refused, a blow from which the League does not recover.

title: Yekatit 12 massacre
description: After an attempt on the viceroy Graziani, Italian forces kill many thousands of the city's people over three days.

title: Haile Selassie returns
description: The emperor re-enters his capital with British and Ethiopian forces five years to the day after the Italians took it.

title: Eritrea annexed
description: Ethiopia ends Eritrea's federal status and makes it a province, hardening the war for independence.

title: Organisation of African Unity founded
description: Thirty-two African states sign the charter of the organisation, with its seat in Addis Ababa.

title: Haile Selassie deposed
description: A committee of soldiers, the Derg, removes the emperor after months of strikes and mutinies, ending the monarchy.

title: Ogaden War
description: Somalia invades the Ogaden and is driven out the next year with Soviet and Cuban help.

title: Famine
description: Drought and war bring a famine in the north that kills hundreds of thousands and draws worldwide relief efforts.

title: Fall of the Derg
description: Rebel forces led by the Tigrayan front enter the capital a week after Mengistu Haile Mariam flees.

title: Eritrea becomes independent
description: After a referendum Eritrea separates, leaving Ethiopia without a coast.

title: War with Eritrea
description: A border clash at Badme begins a two-year war that kills tens of thousands.

title: Peace with Eritrea
description: Abiy Ahmed and Isaias Afwerki declare the state of war over.
